gen-gf-spicy-rice-fs-paquito: Spicy Rice draws every stroke like glowing neon tubing, one constant line looping through wide, tall bowls. Paquito follows in a confident serif, better kept to brief copy than to pages of running text.
gen-gf-sriracha-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans is sharp and refined, its curves leaving generous space before they meet the stem. Sriracha is the friendly, hand-drawn one, while Bespoke Sans handles the plain sans work and isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-sriracha-fs-literata: Literata is a bookish serif, with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones under wide, unclosed curves. And Sriracha's hand-drawn friendliness sits on top, loosening that sophistication so the whole thing feels personal.
gen-gf-srisakdi-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve. Next to Srisakdi's hairline-free, constant-width display letters, its strokes thicken and thin in small, gentle steps, and that gap is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-stalinist-one-fs-paquito: Paquito is a confident, approachable classic serif. Stalinist One does its best work with loose, brush-like tall rounded letters in display sizes, while Paquito keeps the lines close to the caps and isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-supermercado-one-fs-paquito: Supermercado One has a lowercase thick as pencil lead. Its commanding weight against Paquito's approachable classic serif is the pair's strongest quality, and the body is made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-swanky-and-moo-moo-archivo: Relaxed and inviting, Swanky and Moo Moo writes like casual pen on paper, its capitals barely taller than the lowercase around them. Archivo's outward-opening curves and commanding x-height give that looseness a firm sans-serif footing.
gen-gf-swanky-and-moo-moo-fs-asap: Relaxed handwriting leads here, with a fixed-nib stroke that never varies. Swanky and Moo Moo is best for casual, inviting headings, while Asap, a readable sans-serif with open arcs, is comfortable in small doses.
gen-gf-swanky-and-moo-moo-fs-epilogue: Swanky and Moo Moo has the look of casual pen lettering, drawn with one fixed nib and barely taller capitals. It earns its keep big and short, with Epilogue's wire-like sans-serif behind it.
gen-gf-swanky-and-moo-moo-fs-erode: Erode is an editorial, dignified classic serif with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. And Swanky and Moo Moo is the marker-traced, relaxed one, best in headings, while Erode isn't meant for long paragraphs.
